environment.servingMode: Vite development server with direct /@fs source imports; no production bundle used
environment.competingLoad: Exclusive task GPU window; no other GPU work intentionally started by collaborating agents, machine-wide load uncontrolled.

scenario.rendering: Real light-DOM headings, actual DOM text-mask bindings, real canvas contexts, one shared GPU device and one submit per rAF. Explicit field.beforeFrame/render calls bypass idle gates for a conservative all-live workload. No simulation updates are applied to either analytic assembly preset. The mixed page includes three T1 effects and only one T3 assembly field.
scenario.progress: Authored --hgpu-progress:0.5 keeps shimmer, reveal and assembly mid-transition; other parameters use defaults or assemble-and-hold preset values. Both assembly presets contain at most 8192 particles.
scenario.initialization: Dynamic imports, GPU acquisition, DOM attachment readiness and first valid-mask frame are reported separately. Three rAFs settle canvas/DOM resize before first rendering. Scheduler is paused before attachment creation, so JFA runs once on the final DOM mask; first-frame JFA timestamp sum and actual pass counts are recorded. Startup queue work and first-frame work are excluded from steady-state samples.
scenario.cpu: CPU encode includes CSS polling, frame/parameter writes, input preparation, effect passes and canvas resolves. CPU encode+submit additionally includes profiler query resolution and shared queue submit.
scenario.completion: CPU encode start through queue.onSubmittedWorkDone callback after one shared submission. This includes CPU and callback latency; it is not pure GPU execution. Timestamp settlement is outside this interval.
scenario.gpu: Optional timestamp-query pass interval sums, retained as total, effect-only and canvas-resolve summaries; these are not command-buffer wall durations and can differ from completion. Pass summaries and per-frame scalar summaries are retained without repeating raw per-pass data.
scenario.caching: Actual jfa-* pass instrumentation proves one seed/distance build on first valid-mask frame and zero JFA work throughout warmup and measured frames, even when timestamp-query is unavailable. Distance tap version is also checked across capture.
scenario.gates: General per-field summed effect+canvas-resolve GPU p95 <=0.5ms Chrome and <=1.5ms WebKit; Cached glow item <=0.3ms in either engine reported both with resolve and effect-only. Four-field mixed page CPU-start-to-completion p95 <=4ms. Compilation, initialization and first JFA are excluded from steady-state gates. Failed/unavailable gates remain explicit; execution/cache/errors throw after saving the partial capture.
scenario.memory: Logical allocation bytes, not VRAM. DOM mask/raster font constraints remain in the effect notes; morph assembly retains its local raster target font rather than claiming exact DOM glyph alignment.
